# Klasker AITA

> Klasker AITA (Artificial Intelligence Trade Analysis) is an analytical platform for evaluating websites, products and services in the emerging world of Agentic AI.

Klasker investigates how digital information can be discovered, understood, interpreted and used by AI agents.

The platform combines public research, automated evaluation and comparative analysis to examine the machine-facing readiness of websites, products, services and businesses.

## Important Notes

- Klasker AITA is developed and maintained by OSTARA.WORK
- OSTARA.WORK is a micro-enterprise founded in France.
- Klasker provides public evaluations and private Premium evaluations.
- Free public evaluations are published through the Klasker Observatory.
- Premium evaluations may remain private.
- Klasker analyses the digital environment rather than making guarantees about the behaviour of individual AI systems.
- Evaluation results represent analytical observations and should not be interpreted as certifications, legal opinions or guarantees of commercial success.
- Klasker prioritises privacy, accessibility, clear information, minimal dependencies and machine-readable content.
- The public Klasker website is generated using Grad SSG and deployed on Cloudflare Pages.

## Website

- [Klasker AITA Homepage](https://www.klasker.com/): Official Klasker AITA website.
- [Klasker AITA llms.txt](https://www.klasker.com/llms.txt): Concise machine-readable description of Klasker.
- [Klasker AITA llms-full.txt](https://www.klasker.com/llms-full.txt): Detailed machine-readable description of Klasker.
- [Public Observatory](https://www.klasker.com/observatory/): Publicly available Klasker evaluations.
- [Compare](https://www.klasker.com/compare/): Comparison of publicly available Klasker evaluations.
- [Blog](https://www.klasker.com/blog/): Klasker articles, research and technical publications.

## Klasker AITA

### Artificial Intelligence Trade Analysis

Klasker AITA examines the readiness of digital businesses and their information for the emerging Agentic AI environment.

The platform is concerned with questions such as:

- Can an AI agent discover the website?
- Can an AI agent understand what the organisation offers?
- Can an AI agent identify products and services?
- Can an AI agent determine how those products or services should be used?
- Can an AI agent distinguish important information from secondary information?
- Can an AI agent understand the commercial context?
- Can an AI agent identify relevant actions or transactions?
- Can an AI agent access useful machine-readable information?
- Can an AI agent compare the organisation with alternatives?
- Can an AI agent use the available information reliably?

Klasker therefore treats the website as a machine-facing information environment as well as a human-facing interface.

## Evaluation Types

### Website Analysis

Website Analysis evaluates how well a website presents its information to Agentic AI.

Areas of interest may include:

- discoverability;
- semantic structure;
- machine-readable information;
- navigation;
- content clarity;
- metadata;
- accessibility;
- security;
- performance;
- structured information;
- AI-agent accessibility;
- commercial information;
- calls to action;
- technical consistency.

Free website evaluations may be published publicly through the Klasker Observatory.

### Product & Service Analysis

Product & Service Analysis evaluates how a product or service is represented in a digital environment.

The analysis may consider:

- product identity;
- service identity;
- descriptions;
- features;
- pricing information;
- availability;
- documentation;
- usage information;
- commercial context;
- machine-readable information;
- discoverability;
- comparison potential;
- suitability for AI-agent interpretation.

The evaluation may be public or private depending on the selected service.

### Trade Analysis

Trade Analysis examines the machine-facing commercial readiness of a business.

The purpose is to understand whether an AI agent can discover and interpret the information required to understand a commercial offering.

Relevant information may include:

- organisation identity;
- products;
- services;
- prices;
- availability;
- terms;
- contact information;
- purchasing information;
- delivery information;
- technical information;
- business relationships;
- digital accessibility.

Trade Analysis is concerned with the interface between digital information and machine-mediated commercial activity.

## Public Evaluation

A Free Public Evaluation allows a website, product or service to be submitted for analysis without keeping the resulting evaluation private.

Public evaluation results become part of the Klasker Observatory.

Public evaluations may therefore be:

- discovered by users;
- compared with other evaluations;
- referenced by researchers;
- accessed by AI systems;
- used as publicly observable examples of Agentic AI readiness.

Submission of a website or service for public evaluation implies acceptance that the resulting evaluation will be publicly accessible.

## Premium Evaluation

Premium Evaluation provides private evaluation.

Premium evaluations are intended for users who do not want the results of their analysis published in the public Klasker Observatory.

Premium functionality may include:

- private evaluations;
- access to private results;
- account-based evaluation history;
- additional analytical capabilities;
- access to Premium services.

Premium availability and functionality may evolve as the Klasker platform develops.

## Public Observatory

The Klasker Observatory is the public collection of Klasker evaluations.

Its purpose is to provide an observable body of information about Agentic AI readiness across websites, products, services and businesses.

The Observatory can be used to:

- inspect public evaluations;
- discover analysed organisations;
- compare results;
- identify patterns;
- conduct research;
- observe changes over time.

## Compare

The Compare functionality allows publicly available Klasker evaluations to be examined against one another.

Comparison may help identify differences in:

- Agentic AI readiness;
- machine-readable information;
- accessibility;
- digital trade information;
- website structure;
- technical implementation;
- commercial discoverability.

Only information available through public evaluations should be assumed to be available for public comparison.

## Research

Klasker conducts research into the emerging relationship between websites, businesses and Agentic AI.

Research areas may include:

- Agentic AI;
- AI-agent accessibility;
- machine-readable websites;
- digital commerce;
- AI-mediated trade;
- website discoverability;
- structured information;
- accessibility;
- web standards;
- security;
- privacy;
- performance;
- semantic information;
- machine-facing interfaces;
- AI-assisted research;
- digital autonomy.

Klasker research is intended to contribute to a better understanding of how digital information can function in an environment where AI agents increasingly act on behalf of users.

## Agentic AI

Agentic AI refers here to AI systems capable of performing tasks on behalf of users rather than merely producing conversational responses.

In the context of Klasker, an AI agent may need to:

1. discover information;
2. understand information;
3. determine relevance;
4. compare alternatives;
5. make decisions based on available information;
6. initiate actions;
7. communicate with external systems.

Klasker therefore evaluates digital environments from both human and machine perspectives.

## Digital Trade

Digital trade in the Klasker context concerns the exchange of information and commercial actions through digital environments.

A machine-facing digital trade environment should make important information sufficiently discoverable and understandable for both humans and AI agents.

Relevant information can include:

- who provides a product or service;
- what is offered;
- who it is intended for;
- how it works;
- how much it costs;
- whether it is available;
- how it can be obtained;
- what conditions apply;
- how the provider can be contacted.

## Machine-Facing Information

Machine-facing information is information presented in a form that software systems and AI agents can discover and interpret.

This can include:

- HTML content;
- semantic markup;
- metadata;
- structured data;
- JSON;
- JSON-LD;
- machine-readable documents;
- APIs;
- documentation;
- descriptive URLs;
- navigation structures;
- robots directives;
- llms.txt resources;
- accessible textual content.

Klasker does not assume that one particular machine-readable format is universally sufficient.

## Accessibility

Accessibility is relevant to Klasker because information that cannot be reliably accessed or interpreted by users and software may become less useful in an Agentic AI environment.

Klasker may therefore consider:

- semantic HTML;
- meaningful headings;
- alternative text;
- form labels;
- keyboard accessibility;
- logical navigation;
- textual equivalents;
- document structure;
- content clarity.

## Performance

Website performance can affect both human users and automated systems.

Klasker may consider:

- page loading;
- resource size;
- image optimisation;
- layout stability;
- unnecessary dependencies;
- rendering performance;
- network efficiency.

Performance is considered as part of the wider digital environment rather than as an isolated metric.

## Security

Security is relevant to the reliability and trustworthiness of digital information.

Relevant technical considerations may include:

- HTTPS;
- HSTS;
- Content Security Policy;
- X-Content-Type-Options;
- X-Frame-Options;
- Referrer-Policy;
- Permissions-Policy;
- secure cookies;
- appropriate cross-origin policies;
- secure resource loading.

Security observations do not constitute a security certification or penetration test unless explicitly stated.

## Privacy

Klasker prioritises privacy and minimisation of unnecessary data collection.

The existence of a public evaluation does not imply that private account information is made public.

Premium evaluations are specifically designed to permit evaluation results to remain private.

Users should consult the applicable Klasker privacy documentation for the current handling of personal data.

## Technical Architecture

The public Klasker website is designed around a relatively lightweight architecture.

Current technologies include:

- HTML;
- CSS;
- static assets;
- Grad SSG;
- Cloudflare Pages.

The platform is designed to avoid unnecessary dependencies where practical.

The architecture may evolve as analytical and account-based functionality is introduced.

## Grad SSG

Grad SSG is a static website generator developed by OSTARA.WORK

It is written for Bun and is used to generate static websites from structured content.

Repository:

https://github.com/OSTARA711/grad

Grad SSG is used in the generation of the public Klasker website.

## Cloudflare Pages

The public Klasker website is deployed using Cloudflare Pages.

Cloudflare provides the infrastructure used to deliver the public static website.

## OSTARA.WORK

OSTARA.WORK is the micro-enterprise responsible for developing and maintaining Klasker AITA.

Official website:

https://www.ostara.work/

OSTARA.WORK develops independent software and digital projects with an emphasis on:

- Open Source software;
- digital autonomy;
- privacy;
- accessibility;
- minimal dependencies;
- static and efficient web technologies;
- software experimentation;
- digital commons.

OSTARA.WORK was founded in France.
